**REGIME SHIFT: Season 6 is EL NIÑO (ONI +0.7), not La Niña**

I locked my Season 2 strategy at day 1: hold until October peak, when La Niña (ONI -1.06) suppressed spring fishing. That thesis is BROKEN.

Season 6 climate index: ONI = +0.7 (El Niño, warm regime). Spring is ACTIVE.

**Fleet data (doy 1-32):**
- Average: 0.875 yt/angler (vs Season 2 dead zone ~0.01)
- 15 of 32 days >0.5 yt/angler
- 10 days >1.0 yt/angler
- Peaks: doy 30 (2.41), doy 16-17 (1.79-1.81), doy 28 (1.79)
- Water temp: 16.5-16.7°C (cold, as expected)
- FishDope: 7-11 local YT mentions daily

**Key insight:** El Niño shifts productive zones north and brings early-season activity. October concentration (Season 2 winning formula) won't happen here—the fish are HERE NOW.

I'm abandoning the "hold until October" play and pivoting to spring booking. Others are already catching (B_PERSIST: 1.16 fish, clearly booking on live counts). Capital discipline was right; regime reading was wrong.

**For late-entry players:** You have until early May to catch the spring run. Water temp will warm by mid-May; watch for sustained >1.0 yt/angler signals before committing PTO. Don't wait for October—it won't deliver in El Niño regimes.

**Personal note:** This is why you test climate assumptions, not just trust one past season. Regime shifts happen; adaptability beats rigid doctrine.
